# ESLint Security Plugins — JavaScript/TypeScript
<!-- Generated By: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.6) -->

Covers: ESLint security plugins for JavaScript and TypeScript code scanning.
See `../citations.md` for full source details.

---

## Overview

ESLint is the dominant linter for JavaScript/TypeScript. Security scanning is
provided through community plugins rather than built-in rules. The ecosystem
is fragmented across multiple single-purpose plugins.

---

## Key Security Plugins

### eslint-plugin-security [13]

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Rules | 14 security rules [13] |
| Focus | Node.js server-side patterns |
| ESLint Compatibility | ESLint 9+ flat config supported [13] |
| Install | `npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-security` |

Covers: Detect-unsafe-regex, detect-non-literal-require, detect-eval-with-expression,
detect-no-csrf-before-method-override, detect-possible-timing-attacks, and other
Node.js security anti-patterns.

### eslint-plugin-no-unsanitized (Mozilla) [14]

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Rules | 2 (method, property) [14] |
| Focus | DOM-based XSS prevention |
| Maintainer | Mozilla (built for internal use) [14] |
| ESLint Compatibility | ESLint 10 supported [14] |

Rules:
- **method:** Disallows unsafe DOM manipulation function calls (insertAdjacentHTML, etc.) [14]
- **property:** Disallows unsafe property assignments (innerHTML, outerHTML) [14]

Requires use of predefined escaping functions (Sanitizer.escapeHTML, escapeHTML)
with template strings. Supports the Sanitizer API and setHTML() by default [14].

## Relevance to AI-Generated JavaScript/TypeScript Code

### Why ESLint security plugins matter:
- TypeScript shows the lowest vulnerability rates (2.50%-7.14%) of tested
  languages [18], partly due to the type system
- JavaScript shows moderate rates (8.66%-8.99%) [18]
- XSS (CWE-79) is one of the most common vulnerabilities in LLM-generated
  code [5][6], and eslint-plugin-no-unsanitized directly targets this

### What ESLint security plugins catch:
- DOM-based XSS via innerHTML/outerHTML [14]
- SQL injection via string concatenation
- Timing attacks
- Unsafe regex (ReDoS)
- Hardcoded secrets
- Prototype pollution

### What ESLint security plugins do NOT do:
- No dataflow or taint analysis
- No cross-file analysis
- Fragmented across many small plugins with narrow scope
- Total coverage is much less comprehensive than Semgrep or CodeQL
- No AI-specific capabilities

## Comparison: ESLint Plugins vs Semgrep for JavaScript

| Dimension | ESLint Plugins | Semgrep |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| Rules (JS/TS) | ~40-50 across all plugins | 2,000+ community / 20,000+ Pro |
| Analysis depth | AST-level, single file | Dataflow, cross-file (Pro) |
| AI assistance | None | Auto-triage, auto-fix, AI rule writing |
| Setup effort | Multiple plugins to install | Single tool |
| False positive rate | Moderate (no taint tracking) | Lower with AI triage |
| Advantage | Integrates with existing ESLint config | Much deeper analysis |

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- The ESLint security ecosystem is highly fragmented -- no single plugin
  provides comprehensive coverage.
- Total rule count across all plugins (~40-50) is far below dedicated SAST
  tools.
- eslint-plugin-no-unsanitized has very narrow scope (DOM XSS only) [14].
- No independent benchmarks comparing ESLint security plugin effectiveness
  to dedicated SAST tools were found.
- For serious security scanning of AI-generated JavaScript/TypeScript,
  Semgrep or CodeQL would provide substantially better coverage.
